acme_sre: Hey team — hitting a weird failure with the embeddings endpoint after we enabled the new tenant-prefixed caching optimization. Some requests are returning vectors of the wrong length and our downstream code crashes. Repro below.

acme_sre: Example error from our app: "ValueError: expected embedding length 512 but got 768". This only started after Tuesday evening.

acme_sre: Quick repro steps we ran: 1) call embeddings with model=text-embed-512-v1 2) call embeddings with model=text-embed-768-legacy using the same input and same tenant prefix. Sometimes second call returns a 512-length vector but the model param is 768. Headers show X-Cache: hit on the second call.

acme_sre: curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"model":"text-embed-768-legacy","input":"order id 12345","tenant":"acme-corp"}'
```

acme_sre: And then immediately after:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"model":"text-embed-512-v1","input":"order id 12345","tenant":"acme-corp"}'
```

jess_support: thanks for the clear repro — looking into logs now. Can you paste full request/response headers (sanitized ok) for a pair that produced mismatch? especially X-Cache, X-Cache-Key, and model name in request.

acme_sre: Pasted two recent responses (sanitized):
- Req A (model=text-embed-768-legacy): X-Cache: hit, X-Cache-Key: tenant:acme-corp|norm:order id 12345, Content-Length: 3072
- Req B (model=text-embed-512-v1): X-Cache: hit, X-Cache-Key: tenant:acme-corp|norm:order id 12345, Content-Length: 2048
We see same cache key even though model param changed.

kevin_infra: tagging @anna_ml — this sounds like a cache keying problem. The new optimization removed model variant from the key to increase reuse across quantized variants, but clearly that can produce wrong-dimension returns if model families have different output dims.

anna_ml: yep — earlier perf patch made key = tenant + normalized_input + prefix_hash (to boost hit rate across minor kernel changes). We assumed all candidate models in that bucket share output dim. Looks like we missed cross-family cases (512 vs 768).

jess_support: Short mitigation: we can flip the tenant "acme-corp" onto bypass-cache for embeddings while we patch. Want me to apply that immediately?

acme_sre: Please do, that's our production traffic — would prefer bypass while you fix.

kevin_infra: putting a hold on cache for tenant=acme-corp now (feature-flag). Flag: ff.embeddings.cache.bypass[acme-corp] = true. (applied, rolling) 

infra-bot: deploy roll started: rollout/ff-bypass-acme 1/5 -> 5/5.

acme_sre: After the bypass we're seeing no more mismatches — thanks. Any ETA on proper fix?

anna_ml: Root cause: cache key omitted model_family and quantization fingerprint. Fix options: A) include model_family and qbits in cache key (low risk, small perf hit) B) maintain current key but add output-dim check on retrieval and treat mismatch as miss (then warm cache with separate key) C) narrower approach: only reuse across models that we have verified share dims.

anna_ml: I'm drafting a PR for option B first because it avoids sweeping existing cache entries and keeps hit-rate improvements for verified same-dim clusters. Plan: when fetching cached embedding, check stored dim metadata. If mismatch, record metric embeddings.cache_dim_mismatch, treat as miss, and populate a model-specific key. This avoids accidentally returning wrong-sized vectors.

kevin_infra: agree B is safest quick fix. We'll also need a migration script to evict any ambiguous keys over next 48h and a follow-up to include model_family in the key for long-term correctness.

jess_support: assigning action items:
- anna_ml: PR for dim-check-and-fallback (target: 2d = tomorrow EOD)
- kevin_infra: eviction job + FF route plan + communicate window to tenant ops (target: 48h)
- jess_support: confirm bypass flag removal once eviction done

anna_ml: PR link: https://git.redwood/infer/merge_requests/1234 (WIP) — core patch adds stored metadata and mismatch handling. Example pseudocode:
```
// lookup cache
entry = cache.get(key)
if entry != null:
  if entry.dim != expected_dim:
    metrics.increment('embeddings.cache_dim_mismatch')
    entry = null // treat like miss
// on miss, compute embedding and store under both model-specific and generic keys if safe
```

kevin_infra: started eviction job to delete keys with pattern tenant:acme-corp|norm:* that have mixed-dim flags. Job id: evict-2026-03-15-42. Logs: "deleted 18k ambiguous keys" (still running - ETA 15m).

acme_sre: Appreciate the quick response. A couple of follow-ups: 1) Will this affect billing? 2) Any risk of losing cache efficiency across other tenants?

jess_support: billing: bypassing cache may increase token costs temporarily for your tenant; we'll monitor and report. Efficiency: the dim-check logic keeps current reuse where safe, so impact should be minimal overall.

anna_ml: also adding a unit test and an integration test where two models with same input but different dims are requested concurrently. Verified local: mismatches now treated as misses and stored under model-specific key.

infra-bot: ci-pipeline: merge request 1234 passed unit tests, failing one flaky integ test (rerun queued).

kevin_infra: eviction job complete. Summary: 18,432 ambiguous keys removed; no other tenants impacted. We'll keep acme-corp on bypass for 24h, then remove and monitor.

jess_support: removing bypass flag in 24h and will validate logs/metrics. acme_sre — can you verify after we re-enable? We'll coordinate a short window.

acme_sre: Please schedule the re-enable in our maintenance window at 03:00 UTC tomorrow. We'll watch. Thanks everyone, great response.

jess_support: scheduled. re-enable at 03:00 UTC, we will post here when done and include quick checks (sample hits, X-Cache header, embedding lengths). :thumbsup:

anna_ml: follow-up note for the team: we've updated the design doc to include model_family and output_dim as explicit cache metadata fields: https://docs.redwood/infer/cache-keying.md (draft). We'll also add a telemetry alert for embeddings.cache_dim_mismatch > 0.1% of requests.

acme_sre: confirmed — re-enable went fine, no mismatches observed in our smoke tests. Closing on our side.

jess_support: closing thread after monitoring for 24h. If anything else pops up, reopen or ping support. :white_check_mark:
